text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Despite millions spent on marketing Norway abroad, the tourist industry faces stagnating numbers of foreign tourists. Now the tourist industry will try to persuade Norwegians to spend their holidays in their own country rather than going abroad.
-Fish traders from Norway and the EU will meet in Bergen today to discuss fish quotas in the North Sea. If fishing continues at current levels the trout stock could collapse.

-Truls Fyhn, former head of the police narcotics squad, says Norway has at least 8,000 drug addicts. He took issue with an estimate made by the social welfare authorities putting their numbers at between 4,000 and 5,000.

-According to the largest banks in Norway, interest rates will stay low next year. After the Central Bank cut the rate by 0.5 percentage points last week all major banks have adjusted their prognoses.
-A research of major Nordic Banks concludes Norwegian and Finnish banks are less cost-effective than Swedish and Danish.
-The market thinks that the Norwegian crown will continue to appreciate.
